dedupe_keys.name: agrimate agent based global wheat market model with the russian 2010 wheat failure attribution runs

description: This model simulates how a bad wheat harvest in one exporting country ripples through world trade, prices and food consumption, and the deposit applies it to Russia's 2010 heat and drought failure. The producer of the deposit is Kilian Kuhla of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, for a study attributing the food security impacts of that failure to human-caused climate change; the model code was written by Patryk Kubiczek. Agrimate is an agent-based market model in Julia in which producer and consumer agents in world regions trade, store and consume wheat 24 times a year, starting from 2007 to 2009 trade flows and reacting to harvest shocks and export bans. Coverage is the global wheat market, with 1,008 factual and 1,008 counterfactual harvest realisations and two export policy cases, with or without Russia's 2010 to 2011 ban. The model code, inputs, raw and processed outputs and scripts are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: one crop, macro regions, not countries, and very large input and output archives. Simulation uses: testing how export restrictions and stocks buffer food supply shocks and propagating harvest failures into regional food availability. Related records: the global food shock trade model (model-global-food-shock-trade) and PyTradeShifts (model-pytradeshifts) also model trade disruption.
